title: adaptive-ttl-evictor-with-stable-compaction-for-paged-kv
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: fragmentation in the paged KV block pool increases allocation stalls during bursty steady-state workloads, especially when short-lived prefixes intermingle with long-lived cache entries. This PR introduces a TTL-aware eviction policy combined with a low-interference background compaction pass that reduces high-frequency churn while preserving pin guarantees for hot tails. The goal is to reduce tail latency from allocator stalls without regressing throughput or increasing write amplification.

What this change does (single continuous description): Adds an adaptive TTL estimator that clusters entries by observed access lifetime and assigns eviction priority buckets. New eviction buckets are promoted/demoted based on online decay counters to avoid thrashing at bucket boundaries. A background "stable compaction" worker walks weakly-referenced pages (configurable concurrency) and coalesces partially-filled blocks into contiguous spans to reduce internal fragmentation; compaction is prioritized for buckets with high fragmentation scores. Pinning behavior is updated: soft-pins now carry a sticky-decay counter so recently unpinned but frequently re-referenced spans are protected for a short grace window to avoid repeated reallocation. Integration with continuous batching: the allocator exposes a fast-path that allows the batcher to reserve N inline pages for immediate allocation to avoid synchronous stalls during hot-burst scheduling.

Testing and metrics: Microbenchmarks show allocator stall incidence reduced by 3.2x on our single-GPU latency-sensitive workload (batch size=1, seq=512). End-to-end infer p95 within a mixed workload improved by ~14% and p99 improved by ~9% at equivalent throughput. Background compaction added ~0.4% CPU on the host under default settings; compaction concurrency is tunable. System tests: new unit/bench suites for bucket promotion, compaction correctness, and a stress harness reproducing fragmentation patterns.

Compatibility and safety: Backwards-compatible config toggles behind a feature flag kv.experimental.adaptive_ttl. Default behavior is opt-in for dedicated/private customers via config rollout; can be enabled in-hosted after a staged canary. No breaking API changes.

Checklist: - [x] Add TTL estimator and promotion logic - [x] Implement stable compaction worker - [x] Update soft-pin sticky-decay semantics - [x] Add allocator reservation fast-path for batcher - [x] Unit tests and benches - [x] Docs (architecture note and config guide) - [x] Perf graphs attached to PR

Related: ENG-4274 (allocator tail latency project), ENG-4321 (KV fragmentation runbook).

changes_summary: Core logic: new ttl_eviction module (approx 650 LOC) + compactor worker (420 LOC). Small changes in pin_manager to add sticky decay counters and in allocator to expose reservation fast-path. Added benches and test harness that simulates interleaving short/long lived prefixes. Docs: new architecture note and configuration options.
discussion: Diego Ramirez (reviewer): Please add a short-circuit on compaction if fragmentation score < 0.12 to avoid wasted CPU cycles. Also suggest a unit test that simulates repeated allocate/free of large spans to validate no regression in allocation latency.
Maya Chen (author): Added threshold short-circuit and new stress test (kv_fragmentation_stress.rs). Bench shows CPU overhead negligible when threshold is met. Responded with updated commit f6b22a9.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Can you add a safety toggle so operators can disable compaction without redeploying? Concern about noisy neighbor effects in multi-tenant Dedicated clusters.
Maya Chen (author): Added kv.experimental.compaction_enabled toggle in configs/defaults/kv.toml and documented operator guidance in docs/architecture/kv-eviction.md.
Evan O'Connor (reviewer): Please ensure metrics emitted for compaction work units, moved bytes, and sticky-pin hits/misses so SLO owners can observe impact.

Maya Chen (author): Emitted metrics: kv_compaction_runs, kv_compaction_bytes_moved, kv_sticky_pin_hits, kv_sticky_pin_misses. Hooked into console dashboards via perf-monitoring team (screenshot attached in PR).
merge_result: Merged by squash-merge on 2025-02-20. Commit message normalized to include ticket references and perf summary.
release_notes: Introduce an experimental TTL-aware eviction mode and background stable compaction to reduce KV allocator stalls and fragmentation. Opt-in via kv.experimental.adaptive_ttl and kv.experimental.compaction_enabled. Improvements expected for latency-sensitive workloads; operators can tune compaction concurrency and thresholds.
